Retkozberencs Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Petőfi út 9, Hungary

Not demolished. Rétközberencs — renamed from Berencs in 1898, though the site itself has been inhabited for roughly 5,000 years — first recorded a Jewish presence in 1836, with 5 residents; the community, affiliated with the Kisvárda rabbinate, grew to 39 by 1880. Several named residents are documented working as stillmen and farmers in the interwar period, including Miklós Stern, Lajos Grünbaum, Lipót Steinberger, and the tobacco- and sugar-growing couple Jenő Glück and his wife. This cemetery, established as early as 1882, holds tombstones through 1940; in April 1944, Rétközberencs's remaining 16 Jews were deported via the Kisvárda Ghetto to Auschwitz.
